name: Battle of Kohima
note: The plan shows the siege and the fight for the ridge in outline, not every position. The compass directions are only rough (the ridge runs north and south, Naga Village lies north of it, GPT Ridge and Aradura Spur south and west). Jotsoma, Mount Pulebadze, Kuki Picquet and the tennis court are placed by judgement: the accounts do not say exactly where they lay. Garrison Hill is not drawn as a feature; the garrison and 6th Brigade stand on it. The 5th Brigade's side of Naga Village and the point of the summit from which the tank was dragged down are not given.

phases.title: The garrison is penned in on Garrison Hill
phases.text: The Japanese took GPT Ridge on the first day and pressed the garrison from the south and from the north, around the tennis court. The 161st Brigade, cut off at Jotsoma, could only support it with artillery.
phases.quote: was slowly driven into a small perimeter on Garrison Hill.

phases.title: The Japanese cut the garrison in two
phases.text: The Japanese took the area of the Deputy Commissioner's bungalow and Kuki Picquet, cutting the garrison in two. They did not go on to attack Garrison Hill, being exhausted by hunger and the fighting.
phases.quote: On the night of 17/18 April, the Japanese finally captured the DC's bungalow area.

phases.title: The relief force breaks through
phases.text: The 161st Brigade, with air, artillery and armour support, attacked towards Kohima from Jotsoma. After a day of heavy fighting its leading troops and tanks broke through and began to relieve the garrison.
phases.quote: After a day's heavy fighting, the leading troops of the Brigade

phases.title: The 6th Brigade takes over Garrison Hill
phases.text: The 6th Brigade replaced the original garrison, and Colonel Richards handed over command at 06:00 on 20 April. The Japanese went on trying to capture Garrison Hill for several more nights.
phases.quote: Miyazaki continued to try to capture Garrison Hill

phases.title: The Japanese defend; two brigades try to outflank them
phases.text: The Japanese held Kohima Ridge with the Left Force and Naga Village with the Centre Force. The 5th Brigade took a foothold in Naga Village and lost it to a counter-attack, while the 4th Brigade marched round Mount Pulebadze and took part of GPT Ridge by surprise.
phases.quote: the other two brigades of 2nd Division tried to outflank both ends of the Japanese position

phases.title: The ridge is cleared
phases.text: Both outflanking moves failed, and the 2nd Division attacked along the ridge itself. Jail Hill and Kuki Picquet fell on 11 May. On 13 May a tank was dragged to the summit and crashed onto the tennis court, destroying the Japanese trenches there, and the ridge was cleared.
phases.quote: A Lee tank crashed down onto the tennis court and destroyed the Japanese trenches and bunkers there.

phases.title: Satō abandons Naga Village and the Japanese retreat
phases.text: Satō left Naga Village and the positions north of the road on 31 May, which let XXXIII Corps outflank the Aradura Spur position. The 2nd Division then followed the retreat down the road and met troops from Imphal at Milestone 109 on 22 June.
phases.quote: This allowed XXXIII Corps to outflank Miyazaki's position on Aradura Spur and begin pushing south.
